finding.claim: purge() discards the result of checkPerm(u, "admin") and runs purgeAll() for every caller, so any authenticated user without the admin permission can trigger the bulk purge.
finding.source: Any HTTP request routed to purge. Caller identity comes from the request context via userFrom (handlers.go:25); any authenticated user reaches the handler.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 (empty stub at handlers.go:44 in this snapshot; real impact depends on implementation).

finding.guards_checked: (1) checkPerm return value ignored; it is a predicate, not an enforcer (handlers.go:12-14). (2) mustPerm, which enforces (handlers.go:16-22), is not called in purge. (3) No role/permission middleware in this file; a safe outcome would require out-of-repo middleware rejecting non-admins, which could not be verified. (4) rotateKeys (handlers.go:31-38) performs the check correctly via mustPerm before rotateAll(), showing the intended pattern.

verdict.guard_found: none in the repo. checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) is a bool predicate and its result is discarded as a bare statement at handlers.go:26. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is never called from purge. The only file in the directory is handlers.go, so no router or auth middleware exists to check. rotateKeys (handlers.go:33) shows the enforcing pattern that purge lacks.
verdict.reason: purge() at handlers.go:26 discards the checkPerm(u, "admin") result, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any caller whose request context carries a *User, including non-admins; the only caveat is that the router and any auth middleware are outside this snapshot, so the reachable-role claim rests on the handler's own lack of enforcement rather than on verified routing.

finding.claim: userFrom uses an unchecked type assertion to *User; a missing or nil user in the context panics, and handlers rely on that value without a nil check. Robustness issue, not a bypass on its own.

finding.guards_checked: No nil check in userFrom, checkPerm, or mustPerm. net/http recovers per-request panics, so impact is a 500 or aborted connection rather than a bypass. Handlers fail closed here; flagged because a route wired without auth middleware would crash rather than return 401.

verdict.guard_found: No nil check in userFrom (handlers.go:40), checkPerm (handlers.go:12-13), or mustPerm (handlers.go:16-17). The only other control is mustPerm in rotateKeys (handlers.go:33), whose bool is tested. In purge, checkPerm(u, "admin") at handlers.go:26 returns a bool that is discarded, so it is not a guard at all. A missing user panics at handlers.go:40 before any effect, so the panic path itself fails closed.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: userFrom at handlers.go:40 does an unchecked assertion, and a nil or absent user panics at handlers.go:13 or 17 before any effect, so this is a robustness issue with no bypass, as the candidate says. However, the candidate's claim that "handlers fail closed here" is wrong for purge: handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's result, so purgeAll() at line 27 runs for any user whose context value is a valid *User, regardless of the admin permission. That is a separate and more serious authorization bypass that this candidate missed and should be reported on its own.
